note: On the criteria as written this is close to a model fit, which is exactly what makes it the most important ICP case in the batch. Successful: he is a physician assistant, which sits squarely inside 'physician or equivalent'. Income: he committed $9,000 at the top tier and stated he has it, though with real caveats — 'it's going to be tighter financially' and a disclosed unstable job situation — and no financial-picture questions were run, so this is willingness rather than evidenced capacity. Neglected_health is a clean match in his own words: 'I've never really invested in myself in like the fitness side at this level.' Not_deconditioned passes on the criterion as literally stated — a former college tennis player who plays pickleball, is 'definitely pretty active', and works with a personal trainer is nothing like the fifty-pounds-overweight gym-averse exclusion. He misses on good_to_great: he is buying pain relief and structural rehabilitation, not an upgrade. Scoliosis, chronic daily back symptoms, two knees just out of physical therapy and a standing instruction never to lift heavy weights make this a rescue case dressed in an athletic history. The observation already recorded in icp.json — that the stated ICP has no clinical criterion — is the whole story here, and this call is its most consequential instance. In the Tyron Giuliani case the missing clinical criterion lost a well-qualified prospect. Here it admitted one, at $9,000, with a spinal condition and no clearance. A screen that only catches the problem when the prospect walks away is not a screen.
